title: Interior Painting
content: Whether you are refreshing a single bedroom, tackling high-ceilinged hallways, or completely redecorating a house from top to bottom, I treat every interior space with the respect and care it deserves. Good interior painting is about so much more than slapping colour onto plaster; it is about razor-sharp cutting in along cornices and skirting, seamless ceiling finishes with zero roller marks or flashing, and creating rooms where you genuinely love spending your time. Living and working around North Nibley and Dursley, I spend a lot of time in homes with real character, from older Cotswold stone cottages with uneven walls to modern family houses where busy hallways take a daily beating. Before any paint goes on, I make sure floors, carpets, and your furniture are thoroughly sheeted and protected, keeping disruption to an absolute minimum while I am in your home. I only use quality trade materials that leave a rich, even coat that stands up to family life, steam, and natural daylight. When the job is done, everything is left spotless, tidy, and looking brand new, ready for you to sit back and enjoy.

title: Exterior Painting
content: Painting the outside of a house in Gloucestershire is about far more than just kerb appeal; it is the first line of defence against our notoriously damp, unpredictable weather. Living right beneath the Cotswold escarpment and close to the Severn Vale, our properties take a constant battering from driving rain, winter frosts, and humid valley air. Whether your home has smooth render, roughcast, painted brick, or traditional timber fascias and bargeboards, exterior coatings need to be flexible, microporous, and applied over a rock-solid base. I do not believe in simply painting over failing surfaces. I wash down grime, scrape away loose, flaking paint, stabilise crumbly masonry, and repair open cracks before any finish is applied. From a fresh, welcoming front door that gives the right first impression to a full exterior masonry repaint that protects your walls for years, I make sure every window sill, soffit, and rendered elevation is sealed tight against moisture. Done properly with the right exterior paints, it protects the fabric of your building while keeping your home looking sharp season after season.

title: Wallpaper Stripping
content: Stripping wallpaper is one of those jobs that almost everyone dreads, and with good reason. Between painted-over woodchip, multi-layered vinyls from past decades, and ancient paste that clings like concrete, it can quickly turn into a messy nightmare that damages the wall underneath if you lose patience. When I strip wallpaper, I take a calm, methodical approach to ensure the plaster underneath comes through unscathed. I gently score and soak the paper, allowing steam and wetting agents to break down the paste without gouging holes in delicate old lime plaster or modern dry-lined board. Once the paper is off, the real work begins. I thoroughly wash off the residual paste that causes paint to crackle, scrape back loose edges, and carefully make good the substrate. That means raking out cracks, applying flexible fillers, smoothing over hollows, and sanding the walls completely flat. By the time I have finished, you aren't left with scarred, patchy walls; you have a sound, silky smooth surface that is properly sealed and primed, ready to take a flawless painted finish or new paper.

title: Surface Preparation
content: Any decorator worth their salt will tell you that the finish you see on the wall is only as good as the preparation you cannot see underneath. In fact, on most jobs, I spend far more time filling, scraping, sanding, and caulking than I do actually applying the topcoat. If you skip the prep work, even the most expensive paint in the world will highlight every lump and bump, bubble up over dust, or peel away after a couple of seasons. I take preparation seriously. That means checking walls for hollow plaster, raking out and filling hairline settlement cracks with the correct elastomeric or gypsum fillers, smoothing everything down with dust-controlled sanding equipment, and sealing porous patches with dedicated stain-blocking primers. Gaps around door frames and skirting get neatly caulked to keep lines clean and draughts down. It is patient, dusty, unglamorous work, but taking the time to build a solid, perfectly flat foundation is what separates a short-lived DIY job from a trade finish that still looks immaculate five or ten years down the line. I never cut corners on prep.

title: Woodwork Painting
content: Interior woodwork takes more daily punishment than almost anything else in a home, from kicked skirting boards and scuffed door frames to sticky handprints on banister handrails. At the same time, clean, sharp woodwork is what ties a room together and gives it a truly polished, finished look. I paint all types of internal joinery, including panelled doors, architraves, skirting, radiator covers, and intricate staircases with dozens of fiddly turned spindles. The secret to great woodwork lies in the preparation: sanding back existing oil-based coats, filling dents and chips, caulking open joints, and applying a high-adhesion undercoat. I use premium water-based satin and eggshell finishes that do not turn yellow with age like traditional gloss paints used to. Between coats, I de-nib by hand to remove any stray dust specks, giving you a finish that feels as silky and smooth to the touch as it looks to the eye. Whether you want classic white woodwork or a bold, contemporary colour on your doors, I make sure the finish is tough enough to withstand busy daily life.

title: Premium Finishes
content: As an accredited member of the Painting and Decorating Association, I am committed to working to proper trade standards, and that starts with the paint in my kettle. That is why I rely heavily on Benjamin Moore paints for my projects. While cheap retail emulsions look thin, spatter easily, and mark the moment you brush past them, Benjamin Moore coatings offer an incredible depth of colour and rich, velvety pigmentation that transforms a room the instant the light hits it. Their advanced resin technology means you get a genuine low-sheen or matt finish that is truly scrubbable and scuff-resistant, making it perfect for family hallways, busy kitchens, and living rooms where durability is essential. The paint flows beautifully, leaving virtually no brush marks or roller stipple, and it retains its true shade without fading or chalking over the years. Using superior paint does not just make my job easier; it means you get a luxurious, hard-wearing finish that stays looking freshly decorated long after a cheaper alternative would have started looking tired.
